question: In accordance with Regulation (EU) 2024/1252, the Commission must carry out a review of the lists of critical and strategic raw materials by 24 May 2027. In the 2023 assessment, tin was classified as a non-critical raw material, partly due to the adopted recycling indicator. Tin is essential for the production of solders in electronics, semiconductors, photovoltaics and defence equipment, and its price rose in early 2026 to nearly USD 50 000 per tonne. 1.
In its review, will the Commission update the recycling and supply risk indicators for tin on the basis of the latest data?

Is the Commission considering adding tin to the list of critical and strategic raw materials, and what is the timetable for the review and the scope for industry representatives to participate in this process?

Can projects involving the processing of tin and other raw materials not included on the EU’s list of strategic raw materials, carried out by European investors in partner countries, benefit from the Global Gateway instruments, EFSD+ guarantees and EIB financing?
